what: KAI's OWN-BRAIN path, live: the two defects that stopped a real generative turn from coming back from KAI's own model provider (opencode-go), the fix for each, and the raw evidence. DEFECT 1: the provider never sent the routing header the gateway requires, so POST /chat/completions answered 400 MissingSessionID while GET /models answered 200 — reachable=true, every generative turn dead. DEFECT 2: KAI_HOME was resolved twice (the Core's data under %LOCALAPPDATA%\KAI, the model credential under homedir()/.kai), so a fresh install looked for its credential in the wrong root.
host: Windows 11, KAI Core on 127.0.0.1:8788 (live, started by the desktop app kai.exe)

shipped_core_artifacts_rebuilt: app/target/release/core/server.js (bundle installed where the app resolves it)

defect_1_provider_header.symptom: POST /chat -> intent=unknown, from_state=false, brain=null, reply="My own model provider isn't answering that right now — http."
defect_1_provider_header.captured_before_the_fix_on_the_live_core:
RAW CAPTURE — taken on the LIVE Core (http://127.0.0.1:8788, the Core the desktop app runs)
BEFORE this fix, with the supervisor's seeded credential already in place.
Command: curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8788/chat -H "content-type: application/json"
         -d '{"text":"Write a two-line haiku about terminals, then name the model you used"}'
Response body, verbatim:

{
  "agent": "core",
  "from_state": false,
  "intent": "unknown",
  "conversation_id": "sess_musv974c_7dhj",
  "reply": "My own model provider isn't answering that right now — http. I'm still KAI and my memory and state are available; ask me for status, what I remember, or what I can do, or tell me to retry.",
  "data": {
    "provider": "opencode-go",
    "model": "deepseek-v4.1-flash",
    "error": "http"
  },
  "brain": null,
  "dependency": {
    "normal_chat_calls_to_hermes": 0
  }
}

GET /independence on the same Core, before the fix, already reported
inference.configured=true, inference.reachable=true, capabilities
chat/stream/structured/embeddings=true — which is exactly why the defect was
invisible from that surface: /models answers 200 without the routing header, so
"reachable" was true while every generative turn answered HTTP 400.

The provider-level raw status codes from that same pre-fix state (the probe in
docs/evidence/kai-own-brain-final.json re-runs it with the fix in place):

  POST https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions   (no extra header)          -> HTTP 400
    {"type":"error","error":{"type":"MissingSessionID","message":"Request is missing x-opencode-session and cannot be routed efficiently. Please see https://opencode.ai/docs/go/#where-can-i-use-it"}}

  POST https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions   + x-opencode-session + UA  -> HTTP 200
    {"id":"0217912181181005b7c5d80188542749d9bf0e4ecbfb37f8c15b1", "model":"deepseek-v4.1-flash",
     "content":"pong", "usage":{"prompt_tokens":38,"completion_tokens":14,"total_tokens":52}}

error.message: Request is missing x-opencode-session and cannot be routed efficiently. Please see https://opencode.ai/docs/go/#where-can-i-use-it

header_sent.name: x-opencode-session
header_sent.value: KIASessionId() — kai-<sha256(machine|user|platform|arch) first 32 hex>, derived ONCE per install, identical on every request and across restarts

defect_1_provider_header.scoping: Sent ONLY when the configured base URL host is opencode.ai (or a subdomain) — isOpencodeGateway(baseUrl). Another OpenAI-compatible endpoint receives exactly the headers it received before (test: 'a non-opencode OpenAI-compatible endpoint gets NO routing headers'). A caller can still add arbitrary headers via options.headers, and pin the id via options.sessionId.
defect_1_provider_header.secrecy: The session id is not a secret (no key material) and is never logged; the API key still appears only in the authorization header.

defect_2_kai_home.symptom: the Core's database lived at C:/Users/DELL/AppData/Local/KAI/core/kai-core.db (runtime KAI_HOME = %LOCALAPPDATA%\KAI) while resolveModelSettings() defaulted to homedir()/.kai, so model/credentials.json was looked for in the WRONG root and the provider stayed unconfigured until KAI_HOME was set by hand AND the file was copied to ~/.kai.
defect_2_kai_home.fix: ONE rule (agent/kai-home.ts::defaultKaiHome) that model/config.ts re-exports, plus the runtime resolving kaiHome once and passing it explicitly down the runtime -> provider path (createCoreRuntime -> createKaiModelProvider({kaiHome}) -> resolveModelSettings). Nothing re-derives a default.

live_fresh_install_proof.setup: A second Core started from the shipped artifact app/target/release/core/server.js (PID stopped afterwards) with KAI_CORE_PORT=8799 and KAI_HOME deliberately UNSET in its environment; the ~/.kai duplicate the supervisor had to create was renamed to credentials.json.duplicate-not-needed, so the ONLY credential on disk was <runtime KAI_HOME>/model/credentials.json = C:/Users/DELL/AppData/Local/KAI/model/credentials.json.

generative_turn.reply:
Cursor blinks alone —
the dark screen waits for my words.

On the model: I can't honestly name one. I'm KAI, your agent running locally, and I don't have verified access from here to which underlying model is serving this turn — guessing a name would be inventing a fact. If you want it confirmed, point me at the config (or say the word and I'll look for where the runtime records it) and I'll read it rather than guess.

Small note: a haiku is normally three lines (5-7-5); I followed your two-line request, so the form is off by convention, not by accident.

hermes_down_test.how: The Hermes gateway process (PID 23464, `hermes -p default gateway run`, owner of 127.0.0.1:8642) was stopped; 8642 stopped listening and http://127.0.0.1:8642/health did not answer. KAI Core was NOT restarted or reconfigured.

independence_question_while_down.reply: No — I don't need a worker to exist, to boot, to know who I am or to speak. My identity and my runtime are my own; a worker is an ability I can use, never what I am. Workers are Hermes, OpenCode, Codex. A worker provides information; a worker does not become the speaker. Internal provenance may still say worker = Hermes; that is correct and stays. Right now Hermes is offline; either way I remain KAI and will say if it is unavailable.

identity_question_while_down.reply: I am KAI. Hermes and OpenCode are workers I can use; I'm still KAI when they are unavailable.

hermes_down_test.result: workers.hermes.reachable=false while inference configured=true/reachable=true; a real generative turn succeeded ('Jupiter.'); the independence and identity questions were answered from KAI's own state (from_state=true); normal_chat_calls_to_hermes stayed 0.
hermes_down_test.restart: The gateway was restarted with the same command; 8642 was LISTENING again after 16 s (new PID 7236), `hermes gateway status` reports the default profile running, and /independence reports workers.hermes.reachable=true, authorized=true (evidence/independence-hermes-restored.json).

defect_1_regression.test: opencode-go: the outgoing chat request carries x-opencode-session and the opencode user-agent
defect_1_regression.asserts: on the OUTGOING request headers captured by a stub fetch — x-opencode-session is a kai-<32 hex> string, user-agent is opencode-ai/1.0, authorization is unchanged; plus the streamed path, the stability of the id across requests and across provider instances, and that a non-opencode host gets neither header.
defect_1_regression.proved_to_fail_without_the_fix: With the routing headers temporarily disabled (isOpencodeGateway forced false), 3 of the 8 tests fail (both header tests and the fresh-install Core test). Restored: 8/8 pass.

tests: KAI_HOME is resolved by ONE rule: the model resolver and the identity layer agree (reference equality of the exported function + the KAI_HOME -> %LOCALAPPDATA%\KAI -> ~/.kai order)

a fresh install: a real Core configured ONLY by <runtime KAI_HOME>/model/credentials.json, with no env var (boots createCoreRuntime with KAI_HOME and every KAI_MODEL_* deleted from the environment, then asserts capabilities().chat == true and drives a real turn to the credential file's endpoint/key)
defect_2_regression.proved_to_fail_without_the_fix: With the pre-fix wiring temporarily restored (the runtime not passing kaiHome down AND config.ts re-deriving homedir()/.kai), 2 of the 8 tests fail. Restored: 8/8 pass.

made_hermetic_because_they_boot_a_Core.why: These tests exercise the NO-brain worker-relay path by booting a real Core. They were already failing before this change (verified at HEAD: 5 failures) because the seeded, working credential made a live brain available to them. They now pin their own subsystemPaths.identityRoot (which IS a KAI_HOME) to their temp directory, so <temp>/model/credentials.json does not exist and the relay path is what is under test. 3 session-switch + 2 routing-relay failures -> 0.
